correctness.rationale: The complete eighteen oriented-arc subsets of bidirected K3,3 were exhaustively enumerated (by arc cardinality <=5); independent face counts including empty [1,18,108,264,252,72] agree. Independently constructed exact integral simplicial matrices; 341 signed unit-pivot chain cancellations split off contractible free pairs in boundary sizes 2..5 in counts 17,91,173,60, leaving free chain modules sizes C1=1,C4=19,C5=12 and all zero boundaries. A spanning-tree triangle-relator propagation killed all 91 non-tree edges in rounds [46,7,12,19,7], proving pi1 trivial; H2=0 then pi2=0. Two-connected 3-skeleton is wedge S3; degree-one Smith-normal-form attachments cancel 3/4 cell pairs, leaving wedge19 S3 plus12 S4. Independent F2 boundary ranks [1,17,91,173,60] corroborate integral ranks, not torsion by themselves. All polynomial-time claims refer to finite 18-arc complex, so enumeration is exhaustive.

evidence: On the homotopy type of multipath complexes (https://ntu.eprints-hosting.org/id/eprint/50523/1/1844094_Smih.pdf): The theorem's graph has directed edge set {v_i->w_j}; the assigned complex also contains each reverse w_j->v_i, so cannot be specialized.
Multipath complexes of bidirectional polygonal digraphs (https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.05670): K3,3 has 9 undirected edges and 6 degree-3 vertices; polygonal graphs have degree2.

Cycle-free chessboard complexes and symmetric homology of algebras (https://arxiv.org/html/0710.5252v3): A subcomplex obtained by forbidding same-part arcs need not preserve the full-complex homotopy type.
